title: Fennel gratin
intro: Tender fennel under béchamel and a golden Parmesan crust.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Remove the tough outer layers of the fennel and cut each bulb into 8 wedges.

airfryer.t: Remove the tough outer layers of the fennel and cut each bulb into 8 wedges.

steps.t: Boil the wedges in salted water for 8 minutes, until tender but still firm.
steps.label: Fennel

steps.t: Drain well and pat dry on a towel, or the gratin will be watery.
Butter a baking dish, lay the fennel in a single layer and season with salt and pepper.
Cover with the béchamel (store-bought is fine), then the Parmesan, breadcrumbs and dots of butter.
Bake at 200 °C for 25 minutes, until golden and crisp on top.
steps.label: Bake

airfryer.t: Set the dish in the basket and air-fry at 180 °C for 15 minutes, until golden.

steps.t: Let it rest for 5 minutes before serving.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Lighter version: skip the béchamel and use just melted butter, Parmesan and breadcrumbs.
Add a little orange zest or a few fennel seeds to the béchamel.

title: Sautéed chicory
intro: Southern Italian chicory, blanched then sautéed with garlic, oil and chili.

steps.t: Trim off the tough bases of the chicory and wash it in several changes of water until no grit remains.
Boil in plenty of salted water for 10 minutes, until the stems are tender.
steps.label: Chicory

steps.t: Drain, let it cool a little, squeeze out the water by hand and chop roughly.
Warm the oil in a pan with the crushed garlic and chili for 2 minutes, until the garlic is golden.
steps.label: Garlic

steps.t: Add the chicory and sauté for 5 minutes over medium heat, stirring; season with salt.
steps.label: Sauté

tips.t: The more water you boil it in, the less bitter it stays; drain as soon as the stems are tender.
Serve on a dried fava bean purée for the Puglian classic "fave e cicorie".
Melt an anchovy fillet in the oil with the garlic.

title: Zucchini scapece
intro: Neapolitan fried zucchini, marinated with vinegar, garlic and mint.

steps.t: Slice the zucchini into 3 mm rounds and spread them on a towel to dry for 30 minutes.
steps.label: Dry

steps.t: Heat the oil to 170 °C and fry the zucchini in batches for 4 minutes, until golden in patches.
steps.label: Fry

airfryer.t: Toss the zucchini with 1 tbsp oil and air-fry at 200 °C for 15 minutes, shaking halfway.

steps.t: Drain on paper towels and salt them.
Layer them in a shallow dish with sliced garlic, mint leaves and a sprinkle of vinegar.
Let them marinate for at least 1 hour at room temperature before serving.
steps.label: Marinate

tips.t: Even better the next day; covered in the fridge they keep 3 days.
Same method works with sliced eggplant, just as classic in Naples.

title: Ratatouille
intro: Provence's summer vegetable stew, each vegetable cooked alone, then together.

steps.t: Cut all the vegetables into 2 cm cubes; peel and chop the tomatoes.
Brown the eggplant in 2 tbsp oil for 8 minutes, until golden, then set aside.
steps.label: Eggplant

steps.t: Sauté the zucchini in 1 tbsp oil for 5 minutes and set aside.
steps.label: Zucchini

steps.t: In a wide pot, soften the onion and peppers in 2 tbsp oil for 10 minutes.
steps.label: Peppers

steps.t: Add the garlic, tomatoes, thyme and bay leaf and cook for 10 minutes, until saucy.
steps.label: Tomatoes

steps.t: Return the eggplant and zucchini, cover and simmer on low for 25 minutes, stirring gently.
steps.label: Simmer

oven.t: Transfer everything to a baking dish with the eggplant and zucchini and bake at 180 °C for 45 minutes.

steps.t: Remove the herbs, season with salt, drizzle with the remaining oil and finish with basil.

tips.t: Cooking each vegetable separately is the secret: each keeps its shape and flavor.
Better the next day; reheat and top with a poached egg.
Use 1 tsp herbes de Provence instead of thyme for a deeper aroma.

title: Aloo gobi
intro: Punjabi spiced cauliflower and potatoes with turmeric and cumin.

steps.t: Break the cauliflower into florets and cut the potatoes into 2 cm cubes.
Heat the oil in a wide pan and let the cumin seeds sizzle for 30 seconds.
steps.label: Cumin

steps.t: Add the chopped onion and cook for 6 minutes, until golden.
steps.label: Onion

steps.t: Add the grated ginger and garlic, chili, turmeric and coriander, then the chopped tomatoes; cook 4 minutes.
steps.label: Masala

steps.t: Add the potatoes, cauliflower, salt and water, stir, cover and cook on low for 20 minutes, until tender.
steps.label: Cook

oven.t: Toss the potatoes and cauliflower with the masala and salt, spread on a tray and roast at 210 °C for 30 minutes.

steps.t: Uncover, turn up the heat and cook 3 minutes, until dry and lightly browned.
steps.label: Dry

oven.t: Take out when the vegetables are tender and browned at the edges.

steps.t: Stir in the garam masala and chopped cilantro and serve.

tips.t: Serve with basmati rice and lentil dal, or with warm naan.
Stir gently and not too often so the florets stay whole.

title: German red cabbage
intro: Festive Rotkohl: red cabbage braised sweet and sour with apples.

steps.t: Quarter the cabbage, cut out the core and slice thinly; peel and dice the apples and slice the onion.
Heat the oil in a large pot and soften the onion for 5 minutes.
steps.label: Onion

steps.t: Add the sugar and let it caramelize for 2 minutes, stirring.
steps.label: Caramel

steps.t: Add the cabbage, apples and vinegar and stir for 3 minutes, until the cabbage starts to wilt.
steps.label: Cabbage

steps.t: Pour in the apple juice, add the bay leaves, cloves and salt, cover and braise on low for 1 hour.
steps.label: Braise

pressure.t: Add the juice, spices and salt, seal the pressure cooker and cook for 15 minutes at high pressure.

steps.t: Remove the spices and balance the sweet-sour taste with salt, sugar or vinegar.

tips.t: Freezes perfectly, and reheated the next day it tastes even better.
Serve with roast pork, duck or bread dumplings, the German Christmas plate.
Stir in a spoonful of redcurrant jelly at the end for gloss and depth.
